--- title: "7 · Genotypes" --- ::: {.cell} ::: This page continues from steps 2 and 3. One line loads the data and builds the library: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r source("R/pipeline.R") ``` ## Python ```python from pipeline import * ``` ::: ## Equations of different genotypes Each genotype has its own equation, with coefficients estimated from the 31 trajectories of that genotype. The sparse models (STLSQ) of all genotypes, fitted to all seasons, give genotype-specific growth rates. Growth rate along the mean weather path, for every genotype (grey) and for the genotypes with the lowest, median and highest final biomass: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit_genotype <- function(g) { d <- make_design(Theta, tr, g) fit_stlsq(d$X, d$dy) } coefs <- sapply(tr$genotypes, fit_genotype) ``` ::: ## Python ```python def fit_genotype(g): d = make_design(Theta, tr, g) return fit_stlsq(d.X, d.dy) coefs = pd.DataFrame({g: fit_genotype(g) for g in tr.genotypes}, index=["1"] + Theta.terms) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} three <- spread_genotypes(tr) mean_path <- cbind(1, apply(Theta, c(2, 3), mean)) # library, mean weather das <- 1:nrow(mean_path) + tr$das0 - 1 d <- data.frame(das = rep(das, ncol(coefs)), genotype = rep(colnames(coefs), each = length(das)), rate = as.vector(mean_path %*% coefs)) d <- d[d$das <= 155, ] ggplot(d, aes(das, rate, group = genotype)) + geom_line(colour = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 0.2) + geom_line(data = d[d$genotype %in% three, ], aes(colour = genotype), linewidth = 0.8) + scale_colour_dgxe("burgundy", "cyan", "blue") + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "growth rate (t/ha/day)") + theme_dgxe() + legend_top() ``` ::: ## Python ```python three = spread_genotypes(tr) mean_path = Theta.array.mean(axis=0) # library, mean weather b = coefs.to_numpy() rate = pd.DataFrame(b[0] + mean_path @ b[1:], columns=coefs.columns) rate["das"] = np.arange(len(rate)) + tr.das0 rate = rate[rate["das"] <= 155] fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 2.8)) ax.plot(rate["das"], rate.drop(columns="das"), color=GREY, lw=0.2) for g, colour in zip(three, [BURGUNDY, CYAN, BLUE]): ax.plot(rate["das"], rate[g], color=colour, lw=1.2, label=g) ax.legend(frameon=False) ax.set_xlabel("days after sowing") ax.set_ylabel("growth rate (t/ha/day)") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](07-genotypes_files/figure-html/07-2-run-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: ::: ## Ranking genotypes For each season, the predicted and APSIM biomass of the 199 genotypes on a fixed day are compared by the Spearman correlation and by the overlap of the top 10%. The reference is again the mean of the genotype in the other seasons. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r ## Pd, Yd: genotype x season matrices of predicted and APSIM biomass on one ## day. For each season: Spearman correlation of the two rankings and overlap ## of the predicted and true top 10 %. rank_scores <- function(Pd, Yd, top = 0.1) { k <- max(1, round(top * nrow(Yd))) score <- function(y) { overlap <- intersect(order(-Pd[, y])[1:k], order(-Yd[, y])[1:k]) data.frame(year = y, rho = cor(Pd[, y], Yd[, y], method = "spearman"), top = length(overlap) / k) } do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(ncol(Yd)), score)) } ``` ## Python ```python # Pd, Yd: genotype x season matrices of predicted and APSIM biomass on one # day. For each season: Spearman correlation of the two rankings and overlap # of the predicted and true top 10 %. def rank_scores(Pd, Yd, top=0.1): from scipy.stats import spearmanr k = max(1, round(top * Yd.shape[0])) rho, overlap = [], [] for s in range(Yd.shape[1]): rho.append(spearmanr(Pd[:, s], Yd[:, s])[0]) best = set(np.argsort(-Pd[:, s])[:k]) & set(np.argsort(-Yd[:, s])[:k]) overlap.append(len(best) / k) return np.array(rho), np.array(overlap) ``` ::: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} P <- cached("cv_stlsq.rds", cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit_stlsq)) base <- lookup_trajectory(tr) days <- c(35, 50, 63, 84, 99) # day index (das = index + 14) scores <- function(d) { model <- rank_scores(P[, , d], tr$Y[, , d]) baseline <- rank_scores(base[, , d], tr$Y[, , d]) data.frame(das = d + tr$das0 - 1, method = c("model", "baseline"), rho = c(mean(model$rho), mean(baseline$rho)), top10 = c(mean(model$top), mean(baseline$top))) } out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(days, scores)) out[, c("rho", "top10")] <- round(out[, c("rho", "top10")], 3) out ``` ::: ## Python ```python P = cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit_stlsq) base = lookup_trajectory(tr) days = [49, 64, 77, 98, 113] # days after sowing def scores(day): i = day - tr.das0 rows = [] for method, Q in [("model", P), ("baseline", base)]: rho, top = rank_scores(Q[:, :, i], tr.Y[:, :, i]) rows.append((day, method, rho.mean().round(3), top.mean().round(3))) return rows out = pd.DataFrame([r for day in days for r in scores(day)], columns=["das", "method", "rho", "top10"]) print(out) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` das method rho top10 1 49 model 0.967 0.913 2 49 baseline 1.000 1.000 3 64 model 0.985 0.908 4 64 baseline 1.000 0.984 5 77 model 0.986 0.944 6 77 baseline 0.998 0.982 7 98 model 0.981 0.900 8 98 baseline 0.978 0.924 9 113 model 0.971 0.845 10 113 baseline 0.951 0.818 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} long <- rbind( data.frame(out[c("das", "method")], metric = "Spearman correlation", score = out$rho), data.frame(out[c("das", "method")], metric = "top-10% overlap", score = out$top10)) ggplot(long, aes(das, score, colour = method)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.8) + facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") + scale_colour_dgxe("burgundy", "blue") + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = NULL) + theme_dgxe() + legend_top() ``` ::: ## Python ```python fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 2.8)) for ax, column, title in zip(axes, ["rho", "top10"], ["Spearman correlation", "top-10% overlap"]): for method, colour in [("model", BLUE), ("baseline", BURGUNDY)]: o = out[out["method"] == method] ax.plot(o["das"], o[column], "o-", color=colour, label=method) ax.set_title(title, loc="left") axes[0].legend(frameon=False) fig.supxlabel("days after sowing") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](07-genotypes_files/figure-html/07-4-run-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: ::: Early in the season the baseline ranks genotypes better, since the order is determined mainly by genotype and not yet by weather. Around day 98 (after sowing) the two are similar, and on day 113 the model is better on both measures. These results are for genotypes whose trajectories in other seasons are available for fitting. ## Exploring the ranking Predicted against APSIM biomass of the 199 genotypes in one season on one day, for the sparse model and for the baseline. Red points are the true top 10%. ```{ojs} //| echo: false d3 = window.d3 // local copies, see js/ Plot = window.Plot rank = FileAttachment("data/interactive/ranking.json").json() viewof season3 = slider("Season", rank.years, rank.years.indexOf(1998)) viewof day = slider("Day after sowing", rank.days, rank.days.indexOf(113)) ``` ```{ojs} //| echo: false { const obs = rank.observed[season3][day]; const ranks = a => { const order = d3.range(a.length).sort((i, j) => a[i] - a[j]); const r = new Array(a.length); order.forEach((i, k) => r[i] = k); return r; }; const spearman = (a, b) => d3.mean(d3.zip(ranks(a), ranks(b)), ([x, y]) => (x - (a.length - 1) / 2) * (y - (a.length - 1) / 2)) / ((a.length ** 2 - 1) / 12); const top = a => new Set(d3.range(a.length).sort((i, j) => a[j] - a[i]) .slice(0, Math.round(0.1 * a.length))); const panel = key => { const pred = rank[key][season3][day]; const best = top(obs), chosen = top(pred); const overlap = [...best].filter(i => chosen.has(i)).length / best.size; const rows = obs.map((o, i) => ({obs: o, pred: pred[i], best: best.has(i)})); const [lo, hi] = d3.extent([...obs, ...pred]); const plot = Plot.plot({ width: 320, height: 320, marginLeft: 45, x: {domain: [lo, hi], label: "APSIM biomass (t/ha)"}, y: {domain: [lo, hi], label: "predicted (t/ha)"}, marks: [Plot.line([[lo, lo], [hi, hi]], {stroke: "#9CA3AF"}), Plot.dot(rows, {x: "obs", y: "pred", r: 2.5, fillOpacity: 0.7, fill: d => d.best ?
